claim: PINCR (RP3-326I13.1) is a p53-regulated lncRNA that is induced ~100-fold after DNA damage.
source: Here, we show that a p53-regulated lncRNA which we named PINCR (p53-induced noncoding RNA), is induced ~100-fold after DNA damage and exerts a prosurvival function in human colorectal cancer cells (CRC) in vitro and tumor growth in vivo.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the induction level and the manuscript provides qRT-PCR data showing this induction (Figure 1A, 1B).

claim: PINCR exerts a prosurvival function in human colorectal cancer cells in vitro.
source: Here, we show that a p53-regulated lncRNA which we named PINCR (p53-induced noncoding RNA), is induced ~100-fold after DNA damage and exerts a prosurvival function in human colorectal cancer cells (CRC) in vitro and tumor growth in vivo.
evidence: The abstract states this and the manuscript provides data showing increased apoptosis and decreased G1 arrest upon PINCR deletion (Figures 2, 3).

claim: PINCR exerts a prosurvival function in tumor growth in vivo.
source: Here, we show that a p53-regulated lncRNA which we named PINCR (p53-induced noncoding RNA), is induced ~100-fold after DNA damage and exerts a prosurvival function in human colorectal cancer cells (CRC) in vitro and tumor growth in vivo.
evidence: The abstract states this and the manuscript provides xenograft data showing reduced tumor growth upon PINCR deletion (Figure 3G, 3H).

claim: Targeted deletion of PINCR in CRC cells significantly impaired G1 arrest.
source: Targeted deletion of PINCR in CRC cells significantly impaired G1 arrest and induced hypersensitivity to chemotherapeutic drugs.
evidence: The abstract states this and the manuscript provides FACS data showing reduced G1 arrest in PINCR-KO cells (Figure 2B, 2C).

claim: Targeted deletion of PINCR in CRC cells induced hypersensitivity to chemotherapeutic drugs.

evidence: The abstract states this and the manuscript provides data showing increased apoptosis and reduced colony formation in PINCR-KO cells after drug treatment (Figures 2, 3).

claim: PINCR regulates the induction of a subset of p53 targets involved in G1 arrest and apoptosis, including BTG2, RRM2B and GPX1.

evidence: The abstract states this and the manuscript provides qRT-PCR and microarray data showing altered expression of these genes in PINCR-KO cells (Figure 4B, Supplementary file 3).

claim: PINCR associates with the enhancer region of BTG2, RRM2B and GPX1 by binding to RNA-binding protein Matrin 3.
source: Using a novel RNA pulldown approach that utilized endogenous S1-tagged PINCR, we show that PINCR associates with the enhancer region of these genes by binding to RNA-binding protein Matrin 3 that, in turn, associates with p53.
evidence: The abstract states this and the manuscript provides S1-tagged PINCR pulldown data showing association with enhancers (Figure 8D, 8E) and mass spectrometry data showing Matrin 3 binding (Figure 5A, Supplementary file 4).

claim: Matrin 3 associates with p53.
source: Using a novel RNA pulldown approach that utilized endogenous S1-tagged PINCR, we show that PINCR associates with the enhancer region of these genes by binding to RNA-binding protein Matrin 3 that, in turn, associates with p53.

claim: PINCR was strongly induced upon p53 activation in microarray analysis from three colorectal cancer cell lines (HCT116, RKO and SW48) following activation of p53 with Nutlin-3.
source: To identify lncRNAs regulated by p53 in multiple cell lines, we performed microarray analysis (Affymetrix HT2.0) from three colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines (HCT116, RKO and SW48) following activation of p53 with Nutlin-3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1—source data 1), a pharmacological inhibitor of MDM2. Using a cut-off of 1.50-fold change, 66 transcripts were upregulated in all three lines (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C and Supplementary file 1). Forty-eight of the 66 transcripts were also identified in a recent p53 GRO-seq study in HCT116 cells (Allen et al., 2014) indicating that they may be direct p53 targets. The 66 transcripts included several known p53 targets including BTG2, BAX, CDKN1A (p21), GADD45A, MDM2 and RRM2B. Four out of 66 transcripts were annotated lncRNAs (Supplementary file 2). Among the four lncRNAs, RP3-326I13.1, a ~2.2 kb long spliced intergenic lncRNA with unknown function, transcribed from the X-chromosome, was strongly induced upon p53 activation (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The manuscript describes the microarray experiment and the results showing PINCR induction.
